name: KY-032 infrared obstacle sensor
senses: an object or hand in front of it
identification: Small PCB with two LEDs side by side sticking out at the front (one clear infrared emitter, one dark receiver), two blue trim potentiometers, a small green or yellow jumper, and 4 header pins at the back.

confirmations.question: Read the 4 pin labels on the infrared sensor. Are they GND, +, OUT and EN, and is the small jumper plugged in?
confirmations.reason: Clone modules differ. The wiring plan is only valid for a module with these labels and with the EN jumper in place.

facts.statement: The module has four pins: ground (GND), supply (+ or +V), signal (OUT) and enable (EN). Go by the printed labels.
facts.source: Joy-IT SensorKit, KY-032 (vendor documentation for the Joy-IT module; clones may differ)

facts.statement: The vendor wires the module to 3.3 V on Raspberry Pi and Pico and to 5 V on a classic Arduino. No supply rating is published.
The signal pin is LOW while an obstacle is detected and HIGH otherwise. An LED on the module lights while it detects something. Powered from 3.3 V the signal cannot rise above 3.3 V.
facts.source: Joy-IT SensorKit, KY-032, code example and description

facts.statement: The EN pin stays unconnected. With the jumper in place, as delivered, the sensor is always active.
facts.source: Joy-IT SensorKit, KY-032, description of the EN jumper
